newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DUNDEE COULD PLAY FOR GERMANY NEXT MONTH - OFFICIAL SAYS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DUNDEE COULD PLAY FOR GERMANY NEXT MONTH - OFFICIAL SAYS.

text.p: South African-born striker Sean Dundee could be wearing German colours as early as next month in a World Cup qualifier against Portugal, a German sports official said on Friday.
The German Sport Federation (DSB) on Friday backed calls by the German Soccer Federation (DFB) to grant Dundee German citizenship.

Dundee, who plays for German club Karlsruhe and is leading scorer in the Bundesliga, has applied for citizenship to the Bonn Interior Ministry using a special fast-track method reserved for cases of "public interest".
National coach Berti Vogts has expressed a strong interest in Dundee.

"We have given a positive recommendation to the Interior Ministry," said Hermann Latz, the DSB's chief counsel. "A decision should be made fairly quickly. I am optimistic that it could be completed before the match against Portugal."
Germany play Portugal in a European group nine qualifier on December 14.

Dundee's decision to apply for German citzenship has sparked outrage in his native country, where some politicians have accused him of turning his back on South Africa and called for the move to be blocked.
Dundee, whose surname and snappy finishing have earned him the nickname "Crocodile", is following a well-trodden path by foreign sports stars who have won German citizenship.
Dundee, 23, has made a meteoric start to his Bundesliga career. He began last season officially classed as an amateur with Karlsruhe but quickly forced his way into the first team.
He has scored nine goals for Karlsruhe this season.
